title: Search and Sorting as Problem-Solving Patterns
learningObjectives: Explain the topic and its assumptions.
Describe why it matters in solving programming problems.
Interpret a small example or trace.
Apply the idea to a new situation.

understand.concept: Searching locates target values; sorting orders data. Linear search works without sorted input. Binary search repeatedly halves a sorted range and requires sorted data. Sorting can help repeated queries but costs time and may alter ordering.
understand.whyItMatters: Searches and sorts are common reusable patterns. Verify ordering, duplicates, and missing-target behavior before choosing a method.
understand.analogy: Find a name in an unsorted pile by checking one-by-one; a sorted index allows narrowing the search range.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the concept; real behavior depends on input, constraints, and implementation details.

explain.narrative: Define the task and assumptions, choose a method, trace it on a small example, then check edge cases. Searching locates target values; sorting orders data. Linear search works without sorted input. Binary search repeatedly halves a sorted range and requires sorted data. Sorting can help repeated queries but costs time and may alter ordering.
